newsitem.title: ITALY: Trial of Algerian in Italy posTponed until November.
newsitem.headline: Trial of Algerian in Italy posTponed until November.

text.p: The trial of an Algerian charged with arms trafficking in Italy and awaiting extradition to France was postponed for the second time on Friday.
Court officials said the trial of Djamel Lounici, who was arrested in 1995 on suspicion of links with the armed wing of the Algerian Salvation Front, would now start on November 6.

The trial, in which 10 other defendants are also facing various charges, was postponed for procedural reasons and because Lounici and another defendant were ill. It had already been delayed in May due to a lawyers' strike.

Lounici is also awaiting extradition to France where he was tried in absentia earlier this year and given a five-year jail term for involvement in guerrilla attacks in Morocco, including one in which two Spaniards died in 1994.
Italy dropped earlier terrorism charges against Lounici and has agreed to extradite him once he has faced the arms trafficking charges in Naples.
Lounici was arrested in Italy after a wave of bomb attacks in France in 1995 in which eight people were killed and 160 injured.
